items.title: [FDD Diary #28] It Worked
content:
Sent a job from my laptop.
Result came back from the desktop at home.

It worked.

Ugly. Rough. Half the features missing.
Didn't care.

It worked.

MVP isn't minimum features.
MVP is minimum experience.

'Oh. It works.'
That one moment.

Doesn't have to be perfect.
Doesn't have to do everything.
Just has to deliver that feeling once.

Everything else gets bolted on after.

Frustration's real name:
the experience I want doesn't exist.

Questions to AI.
AI gave boundaries.
Boundaries became specs.
Shortest path became the MVP.

Frustration. Questions. Boundaries. Spec. MVP.
That's the loop.

items.title: [FDD Diary #29] Not Done
content:
Five frameworks. Thirty threads.
Should feel like victory.

It doesn't.
There's still a thing I can't solve.

The system works.
Spec, structure, tests, UX — all running.

But every morning I open the laptop and fight the same fight.
AI still surprises me.
Still breaks things I thought were solid.

The frameworks don't eliminate the chaos.
They make it survivable.

FDD. SDD. DDD. TDD. XDD.
Five stages. Each one born from a specific pain.

None of them finished.
The loop keeps running.

Frustration doesn't end.
It just gets a better name.

items.title: [FDD Diary #30] Built It Anyway
content:
I can't code. Still can't.
Built it anyway.

Better prompts aren't the answer.
Better AI tools aren't the answer.

What to build. How it should feel.

That answer doesn't come out clean.
You get pissed. Ask questions. Fight.
Organize. Get pissed again.

Frustration becomes the spec.
The spec becomes the system.
The system becomes freedom.

Phase 1: Complete.
